Bill.BriefDescription: Allowing day spas to offer or supply without charge wine or beer by the individual glass to a customer for consumption on the premises.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to allowing day spas to offer or supply withoutcharge wine or beer by the individual glass to a customer forconsumption on the premises; and amending RCW 66.12.240.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 66.12.240 and 2009 c 361 s 1 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Nothing in this title applies to or prevents a day spa, weddingboutique, or art gallery from offering or supplying without charge wineor beer by the individual glass to a customer for consumption on thepremises. However, the customer must be at least twentyone years ofage and may only be offered one glass of wine or beer, and wine or beerserved or consumed shall be purchased from a Washington state licensedretailer or a Washington state liquor store or agency at full retailprice. A day spa, wedding boutique, or art gallery offering wine orbeer without charge may not advertise the service of complimentary wineor beer and may not sell wine or beer in any manner. If the wine orbeer is offered by a day spa that provides massages, the wine or beermay not be offered to the customers until the massage is completed. p. 1 SB 6060Any employee involved in the service of wine or beer must complete aboardapproved limited alcohol server training program. (2) For the purposes of this section: (a) "Day spa" means a business that offers at least three of thefollowing beauty services: Shampooing, cutting, styling, or dyeinghair, manicures, pedicures, facials, massages, and the use of bodytoning equipment. (b) "Art gallery" means a room or building devoted to theexhibition and/or sale of the works of art. (((b))) (c) "Wedding boutique" means a business primarily engagedin the sale of wedding merchandise.
